**Severity:** warning · **Area:** Resume (`RV2xxx`) · **Quick fix:** none

## Message

The diagnostic reads one of:

```text
Keyed state `signal()` is created inside {an `if` | a conditional expression | a logical expression | a loop | a `switch` | a `try`}: the browser adopts keyed state by creation order, so a render that skips or repeats it adopts the wrong values; create it unconditionally at the top of the body
```

```text
Keyed state `createStore()` is created inside {…}: the browser adopts keyed state by creation order, so a render that skips or repeats it adopts the wrong values; create it unconditionally at the top of the body
```

Parts in braces (`{name}`) are filled in for each report.

## How to fix

Create every `signal()` / `createStore()` of a component (or of a hook it calls) unconditionally, before any branch or loop; branch on the value instead (`const n = signal(props.start ?? 0)`).

## Example

```tsx avoid nocheck
import { signal } from "@rivetjs/reactivity";
export function Late(props) {
  const n = props.start != null ? signal(props.start) : signal(0);
  return <button onClick={() => n.set(1)}>{n()}</button>;
}
```

```tsx prefer
import { signal } from "@rivetjs/reactivity";
export function Late(props) {
  const n = signal(props.start ?? 0);
  return <button onClick={() => n.set(1)}>{n()}</button>;
}
```

## When it is reported

Derived resume model only (`resume: { model: "derived" }`, plan M2 C2). Under that model every `signal(x)` / `createStore(x)` call of a resume module compiles to a keyed registration (`_rSig(key, x)`: key = module prefix + source-order ordinal, an occurrence suffix when one site registers twice in a boundary); the server ships the values, the browser adopts them in the same order. A site inside an `if` / `?:` / `&&` / loop / `switch` / `try` is still keyed, but a render that takes another path adopts the wrong values. Warning: the module compiles.
